title: Pineapple Express
full_review:
"Pineapple Express" (Columbia/Relativity) is a frenzied, vulgar and excessively violent action comedy unredeemed by a muted anti-drug message and an over-the-top celebration of male friendship.

Director David Gordon Green's buddy flick sees pot-smoking process server Dale Denton (Seth Rogen) forced to go on the lam after he accidentally witnesses a bloody rub-out by drug lord Ted (Gary Cole) and corrupt policewoman Carol (Rosie Perez). In his panic, he leaves a half-smoked joint of the rare titular breed of marijuana at the scene, thus implicating both himself and his spacey pusher, Saul Silver (James Franco), who takes to the road with him.

Their adventures include a painfully physical confrontation with Red (Danny McBride), one of Ted's minions, and a nearly disastrous endeavor to protect Dale's teenage girlfriend, Angie (Amber Heard). Along the way, they make a fast, unconscionable buck by selling weed to a group of schoolboys.

As written by Rogen, Evan Goldberg and Judd Apatow, the movie climaxes with a prolonged battle with a gun, knife and explosives during which Dale loses a large portion of one ear, an event portrayed in bloody detail with the apparent aim of eliciting laughs.

The film contains graphic mayhem, including mutilation, drug use, sexual humor, pervasive rough and crude language, and several profanities. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
